Q: Backup-restore the current repeat action (.) in Vim A:

In Vim, you can create a macro that will execute any edits you would typically do in normal mode without disturbing the redo . functionality by wrapping those edits in a user defined :function and then executing that function with a :mapped key.

Example

The best way to see it is with an example. Suppose you want to add the text yyy to the end of the current line every time you hit the F2 key, but you don't want this to interfere with the redo command [.].

Here's how to do it:

  1. Open a new Vim window and execute the following commands:

     :fu JL()
     normal Ayyy
     endfu
 :map <F2> :call JL()<Enter>

  2. Now add some text, let's say xxx, by typing Axxx + Esc

  3. Now press the F2 key and you should see xxxyyy

  4. Finally, press the . key and you should see xxxyyyxxx

It is just what you wanted!

Why this works

This works because of the nature of the way Vim executes the redo command. Vim keeps track of the characters of a command as you type it. When you press the . key, it stuffs those characters back into the keyboard buffer to re-execute them.

Unfortunately, a simple q macro works the same way—it stuffs characters into the buffer and by doing so overwrites the redo buffer. The :normal command does this as well, but when placed inside a user defined function we get around this limitation, because he code that executes the user defined function saves and restores the redo buffer during the user defined function.

This all happens in file eval.c and file getchar.c in the Vim source code. Search for saveRedobuff to see what's going on.

Q: Spark 4.1.1 on AKS + Cosmos DB Cassandra API: ClassNotFound without connector, ClosedConnectionException with spark-cassandra-connector_2.13-3.5.1 A:

You are mixing few things here:

  1. Scala 2.12 and 2.13

  2. Spark versions 3.5 and 4.1

Open source connector for Spark 4.1 does not exists, you are likely need premium support from datastax to get it.
Use more up to date tooling like DuckDB or Polars instead of Spark.

Q: DllExport from C# .Net application A:

This is the answer I'd have liked to see: .Net core applications are launched using a native host. Therefore, even if you manage to export symbols from the .Net assembly, they wouldn't be exported by the main executable of the running process.

In order to export symbols, the default native host needs to be replaced by a custom host using this documentation. In this case, the manifest and app icon/resources may also need to be included by the developer, since the native host is no longer automatically generated.

Edit: I made a video about implementation of this: https://youtu.be/IQlXNoq4X28?si=K02vkwEqh3ZAfyzH

Q: "java.lang.IllegalStateException: Cannot start this animator on a detached view!" after upgrading project A:

It basically means that your code is trying to start an animation on a view that is not attached to the window.

Every view in Android has a window token, which is only available when the view is attached to a window. So maybe animating view in onCreate() before the view is laid out, or animating view inside fragment before onviewCreate() or after onDestroyView().

Please explain your code structure in more details if possible.

Regard, V
